previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with recurrent primary central nervous system lymphoma was admitted for his 20th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy as part of reinduction therapy. He presented in stable condition, tolerating the infusion well without acute symptoms. His hospital course was complicated by mild hyponatremia (sodium 132), likely due to interaction between intravenous fluids and desmopressin for his diabetes insipidus. This was managed by holding one dose of desmopressin, resulting in improved sodium levels (137 at discharge). Methotrexate levels declined appropriately to 0.09, and leucovorin rescue was administered as planned. He remained neurologically stable, seizure-free, and hemodynamically normal throughout. He was discharged home with instructions to resume all home medications and continue oral leucovorin for a short course, with follow-up scheduled in clinic for Rituxan and planning for the next chemotherapy cycle.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
